While cleaning a dusty storage loft behind centuries-old brass cauldrons, Khalid noticed a loose brick in the back wall. He wiggled it gently until it slid free into his hands.
Behind the brick rested an ornate heavy copper key wrapped in decayed velvet cloth. Its handle was shaped like an engraved palm frond.

Khalid respectfully carried the mysterious key down to Master Ridha, whose eyes widened with astonishment. 'This belonged to my great-uncle's forgotten lockbox,' Master Ridha whispered with trembling emotion.

Together they fitted the key into an iron-banded chest under the workbench. The lock turned with a satisfying click, revealing a complete collection of exquisite bronze calligraphy stamps from the Abbasid era.
